chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jamhur from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn from his father from Ismail ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan who said:

I was in the presence of al-Rida (peace be upon him), so he said to me: 'O Muhammad! Indeed, in the time of the Children of Israel, there were four believers. One of them came to the other three, who were gathered in the house of one of them, engaged in a discussion among themselves. He knocked on the door, and the slave came out to him. He said, 'Where is your master?' He said, 'He is not in the house.'

The man returned, and the slave went to his master. He said to him, 'Who was the one who knocked on the door?' He said, 'So-and-so.' I told him, 'You are not in the house.' So he remained silent and did not care, and he did not blame his slave, nor was any of them saddened by his return from the door, and they continued in their conversation.

When it was the next day, the man came early to them and found them, and they had gone out intending a property of one of them. He greeted them and said, 'I am with you.' They said to him, 'Yes,' and they did not apologize to him. The man was needy and of weak financial state. When they were on part of the way, a cloud shaded them, and they thought it was rain, so they hastened.

When the cloud settled directly over their heads, a caller called out from within the cloud: 'O Fire! Seize them, and I am Jibra'il, the Messenger of Allah!' So a fire from within the cloud snatched the three men, and the man remained terrified, amazed at what had befallen the people, and he did not know the reason.

So he returned to the city and met Yusha' ibn Nun (peace be upon him) and informed him of the news and what he had seen and heard. Yusha' ibn Nun (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not know that Allah was pleased with them, but then became angry with them, and that was due to their deed with you?' He said, 'And what was their deed with me?' So Yusha' narrated it to him. The man said, 'So I hereby make them free and excuse them.' He said: 'Had this been before, it would have benefited them, but as for now, no. And perhaps it might benefit them afterwards.'
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of excluding a believer from a gathering without apology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) uses this narrative to illustrate the specific sin of *al-istidraj* or divine displeasure resulting from excluding a needy brother without justification, a key concept in Shia ethics regarding social solidarity. The story highlights that while the three believers were punished for their arrogance and neglect, the fourth’s subsequent offer of pardon (*al-'afw*) was accepted as a potential intercession, demonstrating the enduring power of forgiveness even after judgment has commenced.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bni Jamhour, from Ahmad Bin Al Husayn, from his father, from Ismail Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sianna who said,

‘I was in the presence of Al-Rezaasws, so heasws said to me: ‘O Abu Muhammad! It was so that in the era of the Children of Israel there were four persons from the Momineen. So one of them came over to the three and they had gathered in a house of one of them regarding a discussion between them. So he knocked on the door and the slave came over to him. So he said, ‘Where is your master?’ So he said, ‘He is not in the house’.

So the man returned and the slave went over to his master. So he said to him, ‘Who was that who knocked the door?’ He said, ‘It was so and so, so I told him you were not in the house’. So he remained silent and did not care and did not blame his slave, nor was anyone one of them saddened of his return from the door, and they returned towards their discussion.

So when it was from the morning, the man came very early to them and he came across them and they had come out intending a property of one of them. So he greeted upon them and said, ‘I (want to go) with you’. So they said to him, ‘Yes’, and they did not apologise to him, and the man was needy and of a weak (financial) state. So when they were in one of the streets, there was a cloud which shaded them. So they thought it was going to rain, and they hastened.

So when the cloud was directly upon their heads, a Caller Called out from the interior of the cloud: ‘O you Fire! Seize them, and I<sup>as</sup> am Jibraeel<sup>as</sup>, a Messenger of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!’ So a flame came out from the inside of the cloud and snatched the three persons, and there remained the man, awed, astounded from what had befallen with the group, and he did not know what the cause of it was.

So he returned to the city and met Yoshua<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> Bin Noon<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> and informed him<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> of the news and what he had seen and what he had heard. So Yoshua<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> Bin Noon<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> said: ‘Do you not know that Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is Angered upon them after having been Pleased from them, and that was due to what they did with you’. So he said, ‘And what was their deed with me?’ So Yoshua<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> narrated it. So the man said, ‘So I hereby make them to be free and excuse them’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> said: ‘Had this been before, it would have benefitted them, but as for now, so no, and perhaps it might benefit them from afterwards’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Bakr ibn Salih from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mufaddal from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“If a believer creates a barrier between himself and another believer, Allah creates between him and paradise seventy thousand walls each of which will be as thick as the distance of a one thousand year journey, and of the same length will be the distance from one wall to the other wall.”
